reasoning: The standard 'compose/edit' glyph (a pencil writing inside a square box) is universally recognized as writing, drafting, editing text, or filling out a form. It fits tasks centered on authoring documents, notes, letters, or forms, though care must be taken not to overuse it for generic 'update/edit' verbs when a concrete object (like a video or budget) is present.

distinguishing: Shows a thick diagonal pencil pointing down and left into an open square (writing or editing), whereas the look-alike shows a thin diagonal arrow pointing up and right out of the square (external link or export).
